## Learnings (3)

- **Mjaffle-data-coverage** (`demo_database.orders.ordered_at`): Order data starts on 2022-09-19 (Philadelphia opened 2022-09-26), so 2022 is a partial year. The latest data is usually mid-month: check ordered_at:max before any "this month / this year / YTD" question. Treat the current month as incomplete (whole_periods_only: true). Compare year-to-date against the same calendar cut-off in the prior year, never against the full prior year. Stores that opened mid-period (e.g. Los Angeles, Oct 2025) have small samples; flag this when they top a ranking.
- **Mjaffle-money-in-cents** (`demo_database.orders.order_total`, `demo_database.orders.subtotal`, `demo_database.orders.tax_paid`): Money is stored as **integer cents**. On `orders` the columns `subtotal`, `tax_paid`, and `order_total` are cents; so are `products.price` and `supplies.cost`. Do not `sum` these raw columns for a dollar figure. Use the `dollars` aggregation (`order_total:dollars`) or the pre-built dollar measures (`total_revenue`, `net_sales`, `tax_collected`, `avg_order_value`), which divide by 100.
- **Mjaffle-new-customers** (`demo_database.orders.customer`, `demo_database.orders.ordered_at`, `demo_database.orders.unique_customers`): A new customer in period P is a customer whose first-ever order (ordered_at:min per orders.customer) falls in P. This takes a two-stage query. Stage 1 (name it first_orders): source orders, dimensions [customer], measures [{name: first_order_at, formula: ordered_at:min}]. Stage 2: source first_orders, measures [*:count], filters first_order_at >= start of P and < end of P. Returning customers in P = unique_customers in P minus new customers in P. To count distinct buyers, always use the unique_customers measure (customer:count_distinct), not order rows.
